study.notes: 2010 conference abstract (first author Derosa per the study name in the title record; Italian single centre series): 130 T2D patients on metformin randomised to exenatide 10 ug bid or glimepiride 2 mg tid, 12 months, 111 completers (57 vs 54); per arm changes are printed as value ± error with within arm p and 'p<0.05 vs Ex' for the between group comparison; the ± values are read as SEM (HbA1c change 1.2 ± 0.06 percent with n 57 cannot be an SD), to be confirmed in the full paper (companion paper needed: Derosa 2010, exenatide versus glimepiride on metabolic control and insulin resistance); weight given as BMI only (28.4 ± 1.3 to 26.6 ± 0.9 kg/m2 exenatide; 28.5 ± 1.4 to 28.2 ± 1.3 glimepiride), so pct_weight_change empty; no funding statement (investigator series, FALSE provisional); reductions printed as positive magnitudes recorded as negative changes; extracted by the session (S), 2026-10-16

rows.trial_id: EQW vs insulin glargine 26 week 2010 abstract
rows.notes: second abstract in the group: exenatide once weekly 2 mg vs insulin glargine titrated to target, 26 weeks, open label, 456 subjects, per arm n not given; HbA1c primary endpoint, treatment difference -0.16 (SE 0.07) percentage points, p=0.017; body weight -2.6 (SE 0.2) kg vs +1.4 (0.2) kg, difference -4.0 (0.3) kg; pct_weight_change -2.86 computed at reconciliation as 100 x -2.6 / 90.9 (the pooled baseline weight 90.9 kg given in the abstract), arm change not placebo corrected; hsCRP, total cholesterol, triglycerides and ALT changes described as small but significant without numbers (no variance); design consistent with DURATION-3 (identification from the design, not stated in the abstract); industry sponsored exenatide once weekly programme

json.design: two trials in one group: Derosa 2010 (exenatide vs glimepiride added to metformin, randomised, 12 months, 130 randomised, 111 completers) and a 26 week open label randomised trial of exenatide once weekly vs insulin glargine (456 subjects)

rob.justification: Derosa 2010 abstract: randomisation stated without method (D1), blinding not described (D2), 19 of 130 did not complete with no analysis of the missing (D3), laboratory outcomes (D4 low), no registration (D5); the exenatide once weekly trial abstract: randomised, open label (D2 some concerns), per arm attrition not given (D3), laboratory outcomes (D4 low), HbA1c prespecified primary (D5 low for HbA1c); both to be re rated from the full papers

doubts: SEM versus SD of the ± values in the Derosa abstract
exenatide doses not stated in the Derosa abstract beyond 10 ug bid after titration (0.01 mg entered)
companion full papers needed for both trials
the second trial's per arm n (233 vs 223 by the published trial) is not in the abstract
